outcomes.original: Filing step: After CUA and POE permit approval, obtain ASCAP and BMI music performance licenses online, register as an employer with EDD if not already registered, ensure all staff complete California Food Handler cards and RBS training, and schedule the final DPH and Fire inspections before opening. What to say: The ASCAP and BMI licenses are required by federal copyright law to play recorded or live music publicly; each costs roughly $300–$2,500 per year and can be obtained in under a week online. RBS training (Responsible Beverage Service) is required for all alcohol servers and managers within 60 days of hire under AB 1221; the course costs $3–$30 per person. Food handler cards are required for all employees who handle food within 30 days of hire; the online course costs $7–$15. EDD employer registration is required within 15 days of paying wages; it is free and completed online with the EIN. Fire Department inspection (if occupant load is 50+ or if the Entertainment Commission requires it) must be passed before the POE permit is finalized; schedule it after the building permit final but before opening night.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 165 to 420 days. Estimated government cost: $5,778 to $18,800. Notes: This is the time and cost to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, Health permit to operate, and Building permit with change of use) when they are granted. The timeline assumes the CUA and POE permit are filed in parallel and proceed to approval: the CUA catalog entry gives 120–300 days (4–10 months), the POE permit 45–120 days (which runs concurrently with the CUA after intake), the health permit 14–45 days after plan check, and the building permit 14–120 days after CUA approval. The critical path is the CUA (120–300 days) plus health final inspection (14–45 days after) plus building final (14–120 days if construction is involved), totaling roughly 148–465 days if sequential; the range shown (165–420 days) reflects partial overlap of POE and health processes with the CUA. Cost includes the CUA application fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction valuation and fee waiver eligibility), POE permit application ($2,708–$3,800), health plan check and permit ($828–$2,207 plan check, $470 permit), and building permit ($800–$15,000 estimated for small TI), plus business registration ($55–$700) and fictitious business name ($60–$120). Excluded: ABC license fees (if a new/transfer is filed; not in the path because the description does not specify), sign permit ($300–$1,500), music licenses (federal, not government), and employee training (per-person costs). The cost range is wide because the CUA fee scales with project valuation and Priority Equity Geographies fee waivers may apply (the address is in the PEG SUD per the overlays), and the building permit fee depends on the scope of tenant improvements, which the records do not establish. This timeline is to approval; it does not include time to denial or withdrawal. If the CUA or POE permit is denied, the cost and time to that point are sunk, and the operator would need to appeal or revise the application.
